title: What the 1789 Declaration's first article says

body: The Conseil constitutionnel publishes the Declaration of Human and Civic Rights of 26 August 1789. In its English text, Article 1 reads: "Men are born and remain free and equal in rights. Social distinctions may be based only on considerations of the common good." Article 2 says the aim of political association is to preserve the natural and imprescriptible rights of man. The document is a revolutionary declaration, adopted in a specific crisis, and its English wording on this official page says "men." Reading that sentence as a completed grant of equal political standing to every person then living in France goes beyond the sentence. Reading it as a principle later movements could invoke is also a reading. Both readings use the same text. The declaration did not by itself decide who could vote, who could be enslaved, or who counted as a citizen.
